findings.title: Reminders that never reach the Twilio call never get their retryCount incremented
findings.body: The retry-count increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When a reminder fails before reaching `twilio.scheduleSMS` — e.g. the booking has no `smsReminderNumber` so `sendTo` is null, or the resolved message is empty — the guard fails, no SMS is attempted, and no retryCount increment happens. The reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0, so it is re-fetched and fully reprocessed (template rendering, profile lookup, etc.) on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes. That is exactly the repeated-rescheduling behavior this PR is meant to stop, and a missing/invalid phone number is the failure mode called out in the PR description. There should be an `else` that increments retryCount (or otherwise marks the reminder) so the two-strike deletion applies to these reminders too.

findings.title: Unawaited-safe DB write inside catch can throw and abort the entire cron run
findings.body: The catch block now performs `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without its own error handling. The try block itself contains prisma calls (`prisma.profile.findFirst`, the update marking a reminder scheduled, and the new else-branch increment), so a database error lands in this catch where the update is likely to throw again. Additionally, if the reminder row is deleted concurrently (e.g. by a booking-cancellation flow between the findMany at the top and this update), the update raises Prisma P2025 'record not found'. In both cases the exception propagates out of the handler: the request returns 500 and the for-loop aborts, so every reminder after the failing one is skipped for the run. Before this PR the catch only logged the error, so this is a new failure mode. Wrap the increment in a nested try/catch (and consider using `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`).

findings.title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: In the cleanup `deleteMany`, the new second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` (or `scheduled`) filter, so it matches every row in WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 — including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. The first OR branch is explicitly limited to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, showing the SMS-only intent of this cron, but the retryCount branch is table-wide. Today only this file writes retryCount so there is no immediate data loss, but retryCount is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder model; if any other reminder type ever sets it (e.g. a similar retry mechanism for email), this SMS cron would silently delete those reminders. The condition should be `AND: [{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` (and probably `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry increment and deletion threshold
findings.body: The PR adds branching logic that permanently deletes data (retryCount > 1 cleanup) and increments retryCount on two different failure paths (scheduleSMS returning falsy, and exceptions), but no tests were added or updated. A regression here either leaves users receiving duplicate SMS attempts indefinitely or silently deletes legitimate reminders. At minimum the behavior 'failure increments retryCount once per run', 'reminder is deleted on the run after the second failure', and 'successful scheduling leaves retryCount untouched' should be covered.
